newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Dec manufacturers' shipments fall 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Dec manufacturers' shipments fall 0.5 pct.

text.p: Canadian manufacturers' shipments fell 0.5 percent in December, to C$34.22 billion seasonally adjusted from a revised C$34.41 billion (C$34.28 billion) in November, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast shipments to rise 0.7 percent, unfilled orders to rise 1.3 percent, new orders to rise 1.1 percent and an inventory/shipment ratio of 1.33.

The federal agency said that despite no growth in shipments at the beginning or end of the year, strong growth from April to July resulted in a year-end level 4.8 percent higher than in the previous December.

It said makers of motor vehicles and parts -- which had had a strong performance in November, when shipments bounced back from a strike-induced low in October -- were behind the December decline in shipments.

The fall in inventories followed four increasingly substantial rises. Statscan said manufacturers were able during 1996 to contain the rapid inventory growth that had marked the previous two years. The largest declines in December came from the motor vehicle industry, as well as chemical products and aircraft and parts industries.
The parallel decreases in both inventories and shipments kept the inventory-to-shipment ratio stable in December. It had been trending up slightly in recent months.

A positive sign was that unfilled orders recorded the second largest increase of the year. After weakening substantially in the latter part of 1995, unfilled orders were essentially flat in 1996. (For more information from Statistics Canada, contact Richard Evans at 613-951-9834.)
